events.affected_behavior: Kept the first document compact, with each behavioral rule stated mainly in one requirement and one scope entry.
events.rationale: Directly applicable to spec and acceptance-criteria writing.

events.affected_behavior: Drove repository grounding before clarification and reasoned, one-at-a-time recommendations about product scope, configuration topology, and fallback behavior.
events.rationale: The run inspected current specs, configuration parsing, PA composition, and classifier model routing before asking material product questions.
The Gate 1 task did not simplify implementation workflows or define implementation autonomy.
No implementation or testing workflow was specified.
The change did not involve a prototype or UI/UX design.
No interaction model or visual hierarchy was selected.
No architecture or design review was performed under the task envelope.
The spec introduced no preview, inspector, or UI summary.

events.affected_behavior: Acceptance criteria were expressed as operator- and product-observable model-selection, startup, and unchanged-behavior outcomes, without prescribing classes, APIs, or internal call paths.
events.rationale: This matched the long-lived behavioral-spec boundary and reinforced the selected Skill’s equivalent rule.
This was a feature specification, not a runtime bug-fix verification task.
Implementation completion, PR readiness, and CI were outside Gate 1.
The run neither cleaned tests nor defined test-quality gates.
The required premise—confirmed development-stage status with backward compatibility explicitly declined—was not established.

events.affected_behavior: No independent behavioral decision was derived from it.
events.rationale: Although package boundaries were relevant background, repository redlines and Owner replies supplied stronger task-specific scope; exact responsibility and field placement were deferred to design.

events.affected_behavior: The completed spec says an explicitly selected approval model applies after Gateway restart, rather than defining next-run hot application in existing conversations.
events.rationale: Repository evidence showed the PA LLM catalog is loaded through the Gateway’s local startup configuration, and the Owner asked to follow the existing configuration topology with minimal change.

events.affected_behavior: The invalid-model scenario requires Gateway startup to fail with the specific cause that the approval model is unregistered, and forbids silent fallback.
events.rationale: This sharpened the Owner’s invalid-configuration decision into a semantically explicit, actionable failure outcome.
Timeout, liveness, and watchdog semantics were explicitly outside the model-selection change.
No entity identity, routing identity, rename, avatar, mention, or picker behavior was involved.
The task did not change approval-card UI, tool-call timelines, or execution-state presentation.
The change did not concern system-prompt feature composition or prompt preview.
No optional discovery root or filesystem resource discovery behavior was specified.

events.affected_behavior: Kept the unit limited to Personal Assistant automatic approval classification and explicitly excluded Coding CLI, ordinary conversation models, permission rules, approval UI, per-Agent selection, and a second config file.
events.rationale: This directly supported the Owner-mandated product boundary and prevented unrelated expansion.
The deliverable was a single product change spec, not reusable workflow or cross-project guidance.
Gate 1 defined behavioral scenarios but did not select E2E coverage or an acceptance-test journey.
